items.title: Fake Adobe Update Scams Exploit Real November Security Patches
items.summary:
Adobe just released its November 2026 security patches across nine product families including Photoshop, Acrobat, and Creative Cloud. Scammers know this and are pushing fake "Adobe update" pop-ups and emails that look identical to the real thing — same logos, same wording, same urgency. Clicking them installs malicious code instead of the actual patch.

What to do: Never update Adobe apps from a pop-up or email link. Open the Creative Cloud desktop app directly, or go to adobe.com and sign in to check for updates. Real Adobe updates never come through browser pop-ups.

items.title: Microsoft Defender now discovers local AI agents running on your PC — free and built into Windows 11
items.summary: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Manage settings. Microsoft Defender automatically detects 50+ local AI agents like Ollama, LM Studio, and Jan and shows their configured model connections — no setup needed.

items.title: Firefox 160 address bar now shows Paste and Search when you paste a search term — free update at firefox.com
items.summary: Update Firefox to 160 via Menu > Help > About Firefox. Copy any text, click the address bar, and paste — Firefox now offers "Paste and Search" instead of "Paste and Go" when it detects a search term rather than a URL.

items.title: CISA warns SharePoint servers under active attack — patch CVE-2026-65660 and CVE-2026-67279 now
items.summary: Apply the November 2026 Microsoft security update via Windows Update or the Microsoft Update Catalog — it patches the actively exploited SharePoint code injection and SSH workflow flaws.

items.title: Firefox 160 blocks sites from hijacking your email links — new mailto permission control free at firefox.com
items.summary: Update to Firefox 160 at firefox.com or Settings > General > Firefox Updates — the mailto block setting is in Privacy & Security > Applications > mailto.

items.title: Windows 11 26H2 brings Hotpatch updates — security patches without restart for Enterprise at microsoft.com
items.summary: Check Settings > Windows Update for the 26H2 enablement package — Hotpatch requires Enterprise edition and the latest baseline cumulative update (KB5121794 or later).

items.title: Clay Electric outage texts tell you the power is out before your neighbor knows — free at clayelectric.com
items.summary: Sign up at clayelectric.com > MyClayElectric or text OUT to 855-939-3840 for real-time outage alerts to your phone.

items.title: Ventoy puts every ISO on one USB — free multi-boot tool at ventoy.net beats reformatting every time
items.summary: Download Ventoy at ventoy.net, run it on your USB drive, then drag and drop ISO files — no reformatting needed.

items.title: Accidental Payment Scam: Don't Send Money Back
items.summary:
You get an unexpected payment — Venmo, Cash App, Zelle, or a text
message says someone sent you money by mistake. Then a message follows:
"They accidentally sent you money, please send it back." If you send it
back, you lose. The original payment may be fraudulent and get reversed
by the bank, but the money you voluntarily sent is gone for good.

What to do: Do not send money back. Leave the funds untouched and
contact your bank or payment service through its official app, website,
or customer-service number. Do not trust screenshots or messages from
the sender as proof. Avoid clicking links from strangers — they lead to
fake login pages.

This matters: Scammers use stolen cards or hacked accounts to send the
initial payment. When the real owner disputes it, the bank reverses...

items.title: Windows 11 November 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes 1,252 vulnerabilities including an exploited zero-day
items.summary: Install KB5132061 from Windows Update (Settings > Windows Update) — it patches 68 critical flaws and one actively exploited zero-day in Windows 11 24H2, 25H2, and 26H2. Supported versions get build 26300.9974 (26H2), 26200.9974 (25H2), or 26100.9974 (24H2 Enterprise/Education).
